component.name: Missive
component.summary: A calm, private, read-only mail client

description.p: Missive reads your mail over IMAP and never changes it: nothing is sent, moved, deleted or marked. Conversations are threaded, search is instant, HTML mail is cleaned and remote pictures stay blocked until you load them. Passwords live in the system keyring.

Faster checks: a folder with nothing new is skipped after one quick question to the server. Fetching letters ahead of time no longer delays the one you click, and only the start of each message is downloaded. Folder names in other alphabets are shown properly. A --debug switch shows how long each server step takes.

Fixed the freeze after signing in: mail is now checked in the background and a first check takes only the newest messages of each folder. Letters open much faster (the connection stays open, only the text is downloaded, the newest are pre-loaded). A new look with folder icons, unread counts, avatars, day headings and a clearer reader.

Sign in with Google or Microsoft in your browser, without a password: Gmail, Google Workspace, Outlook.com, Hotmail and Microsoft 365. Missive keeps only a sign-in token in the system keyring and is still read-only. You make the client IDs once (docs/OAUTH.md); Gmail also still works with an app password.
Fixed: the compact text size now reaches labels, buttons, menus and lists too (the desktop theme was keeping them at the system's larger size), so the whole interface really is smaller.

Account setup: a welcome page and an Add account screen (address, password; the server is guessed for common providers and can be corrected). The sign-in is checked before anything is saved, the password goes to the system keyring, and an account can be removed again (its stored mail and password are forgotten; nothing changes on the server). Compact interface from the shared toolkit 0.5.0.
Missive starts when you log in: it checks quietly and opens its window only when an update is waiting. "Start with the computer" turns it off (on by default the first time it runs).
